title: FSSAI Bans Select Variants of Old Monk, Royal Challenge, and Bagpiper Over Artificial Flavouring
excerpt: India’s food safety regulator ordered six whisky and rum brands off shelves after finding they violated rules on artificial flavouring in alcoholic beverages.
body:
• FSSAI banned sales of six alcoholic beverage products, including three Old Monk rum variants, Diageo’s Royal Challenge Whisky, and two Inbrew brands.
  • The ban targets products found to contain artificial flavouring, which violates FSSAI’s food safety regulations for alcoholic drinks.
  • Diageo has filed a legal challenge in court against the order affecting its Royal Challenge brand.
  • FSSAI also flagged misleading age-related claims on some product labels.

Six Brands Pulled From Shelves

The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India on Saturday ordered a halt to sales of six alcoholic beverage products after tests found they contained artificial flavouring additives in violation of Indian food safety standards. The affected products span three of India’s most recognised liquor companies.

The banned products include Diageo’s Royal Challenge Whisky, Inbrew’s Bagpiper Deluxe Whisky and Old Cask Deluxe XXX Rum, and three variants from Mohan Meakin’s Old Monk range. FSSAI regulations prohibit the use of artificial flavouring agents in distilled spirits, requiring that flavour profiles come exclusively from the distillation and maturation process.

Diageo Fights Back

British spirits giant Diageo, which markets Royal Challenge as one of its flagship Indian brands, has filed a court case challenging the FSSAI order. The company argues its manufacturing processes comply with Indian regulations and that the regulator’s testing methodology is flawed.

The FSSAI order strikes at some of India’s most recognisable liquor brands — Old Monk alone sells over 8 million cases annually and has a cult following across the diaspora.

Royal Challenge is one of Diageo’s top-selling Indian brands, with annual sales exceeding 10 million cases. A prolonged sales ban could significantly impact the company’s India revenue, which accounts for a growing share of its global spirits business.

Old Monk’s Cult Following Under the Scanner

The inclusion of three Old Monk variants is particularly notable given the rum’s iconic status in Indian drinking culture. Produced by Mohan Meakin, Old Monk has been a staple of Indian bars and military canteens for decades, and it enjoys a passionate following among Indian diaspora communities from Dubai to New Jersey.

FSSAI’s order does not ban the Old Monk brand entirely — only the specific variants found to contain artificial flavouring agents. However, the regulatory action raises questions about quality-control practices across India’s large and fragmented alcoholic beverages industry.
